perspective:
**Harold Padilla’s available information:**

- Harold knows he is a project manager. He felt frustrated and anxious about his project’s progress and believed his team was unmotivated.
- He arranged to meet his friend Arthur Begum, a police officer, at a coffee shop to ask for advice.
- Harold told Arthur his team seemed unmotivated and that it was affecting progress, saying he was at his wit’s end.
- Harold heard Arthur advise him to understand what drives each team member individually and to hold one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood.
- Harold agreed to try Arthur’s suggestion, thanked him, and afterward felt hopeful and relieved, believing the advice might help.
- Harold told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand what motivated each of them. He heard Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each person and work together for the project’s success.
- Later, Harold noticed the team was still not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- Harold told Arthur he had tried the suggestions but the team still was not responding well. He heard Arthur suggest there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold decided to set up another round of one-on-one meetings to uncover underlying issues.
- In those meetings, Harold told the team he had noticed performance issues and asked for concerns. He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension among a few team members affecting work. He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard.
- Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts and consider redistributing tasks, emphasizing that team members’ well-being mattered.
- Feeling optimistic and empowered, Harold told the team he would implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment. He heard Team Member 1 and Team Member 2 respond positively.
- Harold said their input and well-being were crucial and urged the team to work together to make the project a success.

Harold has no access to others’ hidden thoughts, unspoken motives, or narrator-only information beyond what he observed, heard, said, did, or felt himself.
